title: ERC-8309 vantage-authority companion -- verdict (§5 V1-V5)
description: Derived from the bytes Verdict.to_obj() actually emits, then verified against it. §5 binds erc-8309.verdict as its OWN schema, separate from erc-8309.envelope -- two schemas that happen to share a serializer are still two bindings, and collapsing them is inference inside an artifact whose rule forbids it.

x-canonical-serializer.note: Bound separately from the envelope. If the two ever diverge, a table that resolved verdict via the envelope's entry would be inferring again.

v1.description: V1: the policy AND its version. A policy reference without a version cannot be pinned, so the verdict could not be re-derived later.

v2_committed_set_digest.description: V2: a SET COMMITMENT over sorted signatures -- never a count. §4.2 is normative that the store is evidence, not authority: eligibility is recomputed at commitment time, so a count would let a caller assert membership it never demonstrated.

v3_as_of.description: V3: the coordinate the verdict was evaluated at. Empty is nonconformant -- 'as of nothing' is not a checkable claim.

v4_vantage_classes.description: V4: observations by vantage class (§8). Independence is asserted per class here, never globally -- see the envelope's E3.

state.description: §6 taxonomy. §2 requires collapsed forms be UNREPRESENTABLE rather than discouraged: `resolved` is a distinct state, not a flavour of `agreement`, and no value here can turn one into the other.

inspected_set_digest.description: §9: an insufficient-observation state MUST carry a committed enumeration of what WAS inspected. 'Not found' without it is nonconformant -- it is a claim about absence with no evidence of the search.

execution_binding.description: §10 role. `external` means the verifier is NOT in the caller's execution path: it produces evidence, it does not enforce. A verifier ON the dispatch path enforces; one that OBSERVES produces evidence -- and the signature verifies either way, so the distinction must be declared rather than inferred.

supersedes.description: §6a: evaluations are immutable but supersedable. Superseding appends a new verdict referencing the prior one; it never mutates it.
